subject: all life on earth
title: What If You Weighed Every Living Thing on Earth? Humans Barely Register

scenes.text: What if you put every living thing on Earth on one scale? Humans would barely move the needle.
In 2018, scientists at the Weizmann Institute added it up: about 550 billion tonnes of carbon. Plants are 450 of that, over 80 percent.
Bacteria: about 70 billion tonnes, mostly deep underground. All animals together: just 2. Of that, insects and other arthropods are 1, fish 0.7.
Humans: 0.06 billion tonnes. One hundredth of one percent of life. Yet our livestock weigh 0.1, more than every wild mammal and bird combined.
Of all mammal mass on Earth, 60 percent is livestock, 36 percent is us, and 4 percent is wild. Among birds, 70 percent is farmed poultry.
Since humans spread, wild mammal mass has fallen about sixfold. We barely move the needle. Everything else moved for us.

description:
What if you weighed all life on Earth at once? A 2018 census in PNAS by Yinon Bar-On, Rob Phillips and Ron Milo put the total at about 550 gigatonnes of carbon: plants about 450, bacteria about 70, and all animals only about 2, of which arthropods make up about 1 and fish 0.7.
Humans weigh in at about 0.06 gigatonnes, roughly 0.01 percent of life, while livestock total 0.1 gigatonnes, more than all wild mammals (0.007) and wild birds (0.002) together. Livestock make up about 60 percent of mammal biomass, humans 36 percent and wild mammals 4 percent; poultry are about 70 percent of bird biomass. Wild mammal biomass has dropped roughly sixfold since humans spread.

first_comment: Viruses, all of them together, come to about 0.2 billion tonnes of carbon, three times the mass of humanity. Which number here surprised you most?
